claims.statement: Guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES Maven Java publication/dependencies; GHEC data-residency deployments explicitly lack Maven registry, not every GHEC deployment. GHES site admins may enable/disable package types; source presence is not effective availability.

GHEC managed-user organization publishing remains distinct from unavailable personal namespace storage. GHES release-stage reusable is comment-only, not a preview predicate or disablement instruction.

Maven authentication requires an access token for public/private/internal package operations in this guide. Classic PAT task-scopes are required for the tutorial; explicit workflow exceptions use GITHUB_TOKEN for associated-repository publication and granted read access, otherwise classic PAT read:packages for other private-repository installs.

settings.xml maps repository IDs to server IDs with username/token credentials; multiple repositories may map separately. Source instructs a local credential-bearing file but does not authorize exposing, committing or creating tokens; no settings changed.

Repository owner in Maven URLs must be lowercase even when the GitHub account/organization name has uppercase letters. Host, owner and repository placeholders require target-specific resolution and are not executable identities.

SNAPSHOT versions are supported; downloading them requires enabling snapshots in consuming POM or settings.xml. The sample profile activates github, includes Maven Central and enables snapshots; configured flag is not resolved dependency or safety evidence.

FPT/GHEC endpoint example is https://maven.pkg.github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY. GHES subdomain isolation uses https://maven.HOSTNAME/OWNER/REPOSITORY; non-isolated uses HOSTNAME/_registry/maven path. Preserve isolation as an endpoint dimension.

The non-isolated settings.xml URL omits a scheme, whereas the non-isolated distributionManagement example includes https://HOSTNAME/_registry/maven/OWNER/REPOSITORY. This inconsistency remains unresolved; do not copy the missing-scheme example as verified endpoint configuration.

Default publication targets an existing repository sharing the package name; the example com.example:test maps to OWNER/test. Explicit distributionManagement repository URL overrides repository matching and supports multiple packages in one repository; namespace does not prove ownership or permissions.

Maven artifactId should contain lowercase letters, digits or hyphens; uppercase artifact names produce the documented 422 response. Owner-name normalization and artifactId grammar are separate checks, not a universal rule for all coordinate fields.

Publishing edits POM distributionManagement and runs mvn deploy, followed by viewing the package. These examples were not executed; publication authority, scopes, effective repository access and successful behavior remain unverified.

Installation adds dependencies to the consuming POM and authenticates before mvn install. The example uses com.example:test:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT; it is illustrative, not an immutable verified production dependency or license clearance.

The guide permits owner-wide wildcard repository URL https://maven.pkg.github.com/OWNER/* or isolated GHES counterpart for dependencies across repositories. It does not grant access to every repository or provide a non-isolated wildcard adapter; missing permission is not pass.

Outbound Maven getting-started/POM/naming references and Gradle/deletion guides are separately scoped. No dependency installation, upstream script execution, credential/publication change, rights acceptance, accepted control or native enforcement receipt follows.
